story_type: offshore sailboat hoist with a destroyer refueling stop
hook: 300 miles out. The only way off this sailboat was into the sea.
narration: Three hundred miles off Virginia, the only way off this sailboat was into the Atlantic.
Four people were aboard the forty-two foot boat, disabled and adrift on the way from New York to the British Virgin Islands.
It was too far offshore to send a Coast Guard cutter.
So the Navy destroyer USS Ross changed course to become a refueling stop in the middle of the ocean.
[short pause] A Jayhawk crew from Elizabeth City, North Carolina, landed on its deck to refuel.
A destroyer's flight deck is a small pad at the stern, and the pilot had to set down while the whole ship pitched in the swells.
Then the Jayhawk flew on to the sailboat and lowered its rescue swimmer.
One at a time, each sailor went into the water with the swimmer and rode the basket up.
outcome: The Jayhawk crew hoisted all four people aboard and took them to the air station.

title: Sailboat adrift 300 miles off Virginia
description:
On Jan. 14, 2014, a Coast Guard MH-60 Jayhawk crew from Air Station Elizabeth City, North Carolina, refueled on the destroyer USS Ross and hoisted four people from a disabled 42-foot sailboat about 300 miles east of Cape Henry, Virginia.

Footage: U.S. Coast Guard video by Air Station Elizabeth City, via DVIDS: https://www.dvidshub.net/video/319631/coast-guard-rescues-4-disabled-sailboat-300-miles-off-va
